summary: The Events page: a searchable, filterable and pageable log of every event NovaBank has sent, each row showing the engine's score and signals. It calls `GET /events` with the current search text, event type, risk level, sort order and offset (100 rows per page), and clicking a row opens the event drawer from `views/details.js`. Live events from the `live:event` bus are counted behind a **show** pill instead of being inserted into the table, so rows never move while someone is reading or clicking.

notes.text: Header comment stating the page's key design decision: new live events are announced by a pill instead of being pushed into the table, so rows never shift under the reader's cursor.
Imports the `get` API helper, which prefixes `/api/v1` and throws on HTTP errors.
DOM helpers, including `debounce`, which delays a function until calls stop arriving; the search box uses it.
`animate` for the pill's drop-in and `enter` for the staggered fade-up of table rows.
UI fragments: segmented controls, empty and error states, event icons, the panel frame, score bars, signal chips and a loading skeleton, plus the `icon` helper.
Drawers for an event (a row click) and for an incident (the incident link inside a row).
Page size: 100 rows per request, the API's default `limit` (the API caps it at 500).

`row` renders one table row. `trip` is the travel analysis the pipeline stored on the event, if any (`?.` yields `undefined` when there is no context). The row carries `data-event` so a click opens that event's drawer.
Event ID, local date and time, and customer ID in monospace so IDs line up for scanning.
Type icon and label. The location cell adds a red plane tag with the implied speed when the pipeline judged the trip **impossible**, so suspicious travel stands out without opening the row.
Score bar coloured by the stored risk level, and at most two signal chips (a `+N` chip stands for the rest).
The linked incident as a button carrying `data-incident`, or a faint dash when the event didn't join an incident. Lines 23-24 close the row and the function.
Page module titled `Events`. `render` also receives `params`: the query string after the hash route (for example `#/events?q=Lagos`) as a `URLSearchParams` object.

All filter state in one object, with keys named exactly like the API's query parameters so line 53 can send it as is. `q` comes from the URL when the overview map links here, and a `?level=` value is uppercased to match stored levels like `CRITICAL`.
`items` holds the rows loaded so far, `total` the server's count for the current filters and `pending` the live events not yet shown.
Mounts the page markup in one step.
Header: eyebrow, title, a description inviting the user to click a row for the score explanation, and a total-count tag that shows `—` until the first load finishes.
The filter bar starts with the search box, prefilled from `state.q`. The `/` key hint advertises the keyboard shortcut wired up on line 105.

Three segmented controls: event type, risk level (an exact match, so `High` shows only HIGH events; it can be preselected from the URL) and sort order. Their values are the exact strings the API expects, such as `resource_access`, `HIGH` or `asc`. Line 44 closes the filter bar.
The new-events pill, `hidden` until a live event arrives. CSS makes it sticky just below the top bar, so it stays visible however far the user has scrolled.
Results panel. The table area shows an 8-row loading skeleton until data arrives; the footer holds a `Showing x of y` label and a hidden `Load 100 more` button.
The results container that `load` fills.
`latest` numbers the loads, so a response that has been overtaken can be recognized and dropped.
`load(append)` fetches one page. With `append` false it replaces the table (a new search or filter); with `true` it adds the next page underneath.
A fresh query always restarts at offset 0.
Takes a ticket: every call gets the next number, and only the newest may render.
The `try` block covers both the request and the rendering.

Turns the state plus `limit` into a query string and calls `GET /events`. Empty values such as `event_type=` are sent too, and the API treats them as no filter. (This local `params` shadows the `render` argument of the same name.)

If another load started while this one was waiting (a new search, a filter click or Load more), this answer is stale and is dropped. Requests used to render in arrival order, so a slower, older response could show results for the wrong filter, and a late Load-more reply could even crash into an error box.
Stores the server's total and either replaces or extends the list of loaded items.
On a fresh load, mounts the full table with its header row, or an empty state with a filter icon when nothing matches.
Fades the rows up in quick succession: no blur, a 6 px rise, 18 ms apart. `max: 24` animates only the first 24 rows, so a 100-row page appears without a long ripple.
When appending, takes the existing table body and remembers how many rows it already holds.
Adds only the new page's rows to the end with `insertAdjacentHTML`, so existing rows and the scroll position stay put, then animates just those new rows (`slice(before)`).
Updates the header tag (for example `2,431 events`) and the footer label, and hides `Load more` once every matching row is loaded.
Any failure, network or HTTP, replaces the table with an error box showing the message, unless a newer load has taken over. Line 74 closes `load`.
The search box sets `state.q` and reloads only after typing pauses for 220 ms, so a whole word costs one request instead of one per keystroke.
Each segmented control writes its value into the matching state key and reloads. `bindSeg` calls back only when the pressed value actually changes.
`Load more` moves the offset forward by one page and appends.

Delegated clicks for the table: the incident link opens the incident drawer, `stopPropagation()` stops the click from bubbling past the view, and `return` keeps the row's event drawer from opening too.
Any other click inside a row opens that event's drawer.
Gets the pill and subscribes to `live:event` through `ctx`, so the subscription ends when the user leaves the page.
Counts the waiting events and updates the label, for example `3 new events · show`. Every live event counts, even ones the current filters would hide.
Only on the first waiting event: unhides the pill and drops it in with a slight overshoot (`outBack`). Later events just change the number, so the pill doesn't keep bouncing.
Clicking the pill means the user is ready to see the new events: the counter resets and the pill hides.
The page then scrolls smoothly to the top and reloads the first page with the current filters, so new rows appear only when the user asks for them.
Stores a `focusSearch` function on the context. `main.js` calls `current.focusSearch()` when the user presses `/`, so the shortcut works only while this page is open.
Awaits the first page, so `render` finishes, and the router's top progress bar completes, only once the table is filled.
Closes `render` and the page object.
